{{Short description|none}} {{Use mdy dates|date=October 2021}} {{use American English|date=November 2020}} {{Infobox election | election_name = 2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Montana | country = Montana | type = legislative | ongoing = yes | previous_election = 2020 United States House of Representatives election in Montana | previous_year = 2020 | next_election = 2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Montana | next_year = 2024 | seats_for_election = All 2 of Montana seats to the [[United States House of Representatives]] | popular_vote1 = | map_size = | map_image = | swing1 = | percentage1 = | seat_change1 = | seats1 = 2 | last_election1 = 1 | party1 = Republican Party (United States) | swing2 = | percentage2 = | popular_vote2 = | seat_change2 = | seats2 = 0 | last_election2 = 0 | party2 = Democratic Party (United States) | election_date = November 8, 2022 | map_caption = }}{{Elections in Montana}} The '''2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Montana''' will be held on November 8, 2022, to elect two [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]]s from [[Montana]], one from each of its [[congressional district]]s. Prior to this election cycle, Montana had one [[at-large]] [[Montana's at-large congressional district|district]], represented by Republican [[Matt Rosendale]]. However, during the [[2020 United States redistricting cycle|2020 redistricting cycle]], Montana regained the {{ushr|MT|2|C}} that it lost in 1993. As a result, Montana became the first state relegated from multi-district to at-large status that reclaimed a 2nd representative in the House of Representatives, in which Rosendale is running for re-election.{{Cite web|url=https://billingsgazette.com/news/state-and-regional/govt-and-politics/montana-gains-second-u-s-house-seat/article_119b7b78-ac35-5f77-8542-6d3d442ad500.html|title=Montana gains second U.S. House seat|first=Tom|last=Lutey|website=The Billings Gazette}}{{Cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/montana-census-2020-747de9091fc5108e47dd5b97e06642a6|title=Rapid population growth gives Montana 2nd US House seat|website=AP News|date=April 26, 2021}} {{toclimit|2}} ==District 1== {{Infobox election | election_name = 2022 Montana's 1st congressional district election | country = Montana | type = presidential | ongoing = yes | previous_election = | previous_year = | election_date = | next_election = 2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Montana#District 1 | next_year = 2024 | image_size = x150px | image1 = Ryan Zinke official portrait (cropped 2).jpg | nominee1 = [[Ryan Zinke]] | party1 = Republican Party (United States) | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | image2 = 3x4.svg | nominee2 = [[Monica Tranel]] | party2 = Democratic Party (United States) | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | image3 = 3x4.svg | nominee3 = John Lamb | party3 = Libertarian Party (United States) | popular_vote3 = | percentage3 = | map_image = | map_size = | map_caption = | title = U.S. Representative | before_election = None
(New district) | before_party = | after_election = | after_party = }} {{see also|Montana's 1st congressional district}} The 1st district is based in mountainous [[Western Montana]], including the cities of [[Missoula, Montana|Missoula]], [[Bozeman, Montana|Bozeman]] and [[Butte, Montana|Butte]].{{cite web |title=MT redistricting commission officially approves final map |work=NBC Montana |date=November 12, 2021 |first=Emma |last=Wulfhorst |access-date=November 13, 2021 |url=https://nbcmontana.com/news/local/mt-redistricting-commission-officially-approves-final-map}} It is currently represented along with the rest of the state by {{ushr|MT|AL|C}} representative [[Matt Rosendale]].
